subject: Xi-Trump-Putin Summit In Focus

Here's why neoclouds are up.Tech outages: Bank execs and the NSA blame AI-driven patches, while Trump shrugs off concerns.Another flip: Mary Peltola wins Alaska's Senate race, securing Democrats' largest majority since 2009.

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 AI strength: Nvidia ( NVDA ) results lift stock, Huang's return ruled out . Here's why neoclouds are up .

 Tech outages: Bank execs and the NSA blame AI-driven patches , while Trump shrugs off concerns.
 
Another flip: Mary Peltola wins Alaska's Senate race , securing Democrats' largest majority since 2009.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 High stakes 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
President Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders Summit on Wednesday, ahead of his first trilateral meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin. Xi broke precedent to greet Trump in person at the airport, reciprocating Trump's welcome of the Chinese leader when he visited the U.S. in Sept.

 On the table:  The stakes are high for Thursday's trilateral meeting, with talks expected to center on trade, AI, nuclear weapons, and possibly the wars in Iran and Ukraine. This comes on the heels of the U.S. announcing more curbs on China's access to AI chips, after which Beijing threatened retaliation. "The most disruptive retaliation might include limiting China's rare earth exports ," UBS' Paul Donovan said. At the APEC CEO Summit, Xi said China will provide "a more stable and predictable" environment for global investors by reducing tariffs, expanding market access and exploring regulatory reforms. "While he didn't say so explicitly, his message was clear: China wants to be seen as a partner in global technology development, in contrast to Washington's more restrictive approach," George Chen, chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, told the Associated Press .

 Moscow view:  Xi and Putin met on Wednesday ahead of Trump's arrival, with the leaders touting bilateral ties and criticizing Western trade barriers . Putin said he sees "substantial potential benefit" in the upcoming trilateral meeting, calling for partnership and dialogue. "Old instruments of economic domination and de facto coercion have become obsolete," Putin noted. "Sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions may still have a restraining effect, but they are no longer capable of bringing growth to a complete halt." He also took a dig at the European Union, saying it is "losing its industrial capacity and competitive edge." Putin also calling out the bloc's swelling debt, soaring inflation and declining living standards – "a particularly humiliating development." 

 Bigger picture: Optics and precedent will be more important than any concrete deliverables, according to Andrew Peek, director of the Adrienne Arsht National Security Resilience Initiative at the Atlantic Council. "Even without agreement, the optic of Xi and Putin discussing Iran with Trump will likely cause unease in Tehran and suspicion of its friends in Moscow and Beijing," Peek stated. Meanwhile, concerns are mounting that Ukraine could become a bargaining chip in negotiations over a new global balance of power. "Trump's intention to discuss Ukraine with Putin and Xi only reinforces that fear," Myroslava Gongadze, nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council’s Eurasia Center, warned. As for China, Xi faces pressure at home  due to slowing economic growth. Trump's emphasis on friendly ties with Xi may lead to an extension of the trade truce reached last year. ( 2 comments )
